messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD#INC-8721) — P1 ReservedCapacityExceeded for tenant lucent-prod. Metric: reserved_pool_headroom < 5% for 3m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-8721

oncall-alex: oncall here, acked the PD. jumping in.

sre-maya: grabbing initial graphs. are we seeing KV cache evictions or burst spikes? any recent config changes for lucent?

eng-runtime-jordan: lucent scheduled a large nightly burst at 02:00 UTC, looks like autoscale failed to allocate burst nodes. logs show repeated enqueue and soft-ooms on the reserved pool router.

support-sam: customer support slack: lucent reported increased 503s and 'slow generation' for ~4m starting 02:03. they saw ~15% error rate on a small subset of routes.

oncall-alex: impact: partial customer errors (503) and latency > 2s on reserved endpoints. Not global. Looks tenant-scoped to lucent reserved capacity.

sre-maya: graphs: reserved_pool_headroom dropped to 1.2%. queue_depth spiked x7. KV cache eviction events correlated. rolling join logs attached: `router: request queued, kv-miss, fallback=shared`

eng-runtime-jordan: trying a soft mitigation: increase reserved pool count for lucent by 2. running CLI now.

eng-runtime-jordan: ```shell
redwoodctl reserved-pool scale --tenant lucent-prod --delta 2
# response: scaling start, expected node ready ~90s
```

oncall-alex: good. also enable fallback to shared pool if queue > 100 to reduce 503s. can we do that as quick patch?

eng-runtime-jordan: yes patching routing policy: set fallback_threshold=100, fallback_target=shared-pool. Applying managed policy change.

incident-bot: PD INC-8721 updated: acknowledged by oncall-alex. Escalation policy will run if no progress in 15m.

support-sam: pinged lucent CSM to let them know we're scaling and enabling shared-pool fallback. asked for any active jobs they can pause.

product-elaine: do we have SLA exposure for lucent? should prep a comms note.

oncall-alex: SLA: reserved capacity SLO is 99.9% uptime for reserved endpoints. partial degradation here — likely within short window but escalate to SEs if >30m.

eng-runtime-jordan: scale completed on 2 nodes. new nodes passing healthchecks. headroom recovering: 1.2% -> 18% in last 40s. queue draining.

sre-maya: KV cache evictions stopped after headroom recovered. still seeing a handful of 503s in logs but tail latency improving.

support-sam: lucent confirms errors dropping and response times normalizing. they asked what caused autoscale miss.

eng-runtime-jordan: preliminary root cause: scheduled burst exceeded predicted token-rate due to misconfigured burst_policy multiplier (1.0 -> should have been 1.5). autoscaler decision window didn't trigger due to short pre-warm window.

oncall-alex: action items: 1) stabilize tenant (done), 2) follow up root-cause (eng-runtime + ml infra), 3) run retro and add synthetic spike test for reserved autoscale, 4) comms to customer if >15m impact.

product-elaine: creating a short incident note for product/CS. will coordinate comms if support advises.

incident-bot: PD INC-8721 status: acknowledged -> resolved (auto-resolve triggered after 20m of headroom>10%).

oncall-alex: marking thread resolved but leaving follow-ups. tagging owners: @eng-runtime-jordan for RCA, @sre-maya for monitoring rule tuning, @support-sam for customer comms.

eng-runtime-jordan: filing RCA ticket now (RCA-5231) with logs, autoscaler decision trace, and proposed patch to burst_policy heuristics.

sre-maya: I'll propose a new alert: reserved_pool_headroom < 10% for >2m OR queue_depth > 200 should trigger preemptive scale + paging.

support-sam: lucent asked for a postmortem summary — I'll draft and share to the lucent CSM.

oncall-alex: thanks team. final note: no global impact, tenant-scoped, mitigation successful with scale + fallback. closing. :white_check_mark:
